experiment: E20 R4/R5: TraPrInq / McCATMuS fine-tuned on the rebuilt st_c1m training lines
recipe: ketos -s 42 train -f binary -i INIT -B 16 --accumulate-grad-batches 1 -r LR --augment -q fixed -N 20 -p 0.9 -u NFD --resize union --precision 16-mixed (T4; st_c1m was bf16-mixed on an L4)

data.validation: ketos -p 0.9: 243 of the 2,425 lines, random_split seeded 42 (kraken/train/vgsl.py:138); no evaluation page is involved

rule: lr chosen per recognizer by best validation accuracy, from {Kraken default 1e-3, 1e-4, 3e-4}; validation accuracy is compared only within one recognizer
caveats: train.arrow is not byte-identical across VMs (sha256 14439956... on e20p, b1279c26... on e20p4, c32b8f35... in the smoke): ketos compile --workers 2 writes pages in pool.imap_unordered order (kraken/lib/arrow_dataset.py:290), so the seeded 90/10 split holds out a different 243 lines on each VM. The line set is identical; the three lrs of one recognizer share one arrow, so the lr choice is consistent, but validation accuracy is not comparable across recognizers or with st_c1m. Recognizers are compared by WER on the tuning pages.
r5_mccatmus_lr3e-4 and r4 lr1e-4 / r5 lr1e-4 peaked at the last or second-to-last epoch; the 20-epoch budget is kept equal to st_c1m and not extended.

Training ran on Colab T4: TraPrInq on e20p (pro), McCATMuS on e20p4 (pro) after free VMs e20p2/e20p3 were reclaimed before finishing a run; peak GPU 10,747 MB at batch 16 (e20p4), 3,788 s for the 3 McCATMuS runs.
